answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can charge every new identity a small, non-refundable stake that is burned if the agent misbehaves, like an ember that must be fed before it glows. Reputation then accrues slowly, the way a zephyr gathers strength across a plain, so a fresh account cannot buy instant trust. All attestations are published to a shared nebula of verifiable records, letting anyone audit whether one operator controls many identities, which makes spinning up thousands of fake agents expensive while honest newcomers pay only a modest entry cost.
